item.description:
Glow 3.0 is the first release built on a rewritten core: one codebase behind both macOS 26 and macOS 27, in place of a separate build for each. Almost none of that work is visible, which is why this release took a while and why it is light on new features. What is new here is chiefly the redesigned Settings and Moods, a much faster way to change how your menu bar looks. It is still being polished.

✨ New

  • Settings has been rebuilt: a new structure and navigation, search that reaches every pane, and a Native accent mode that draws real system components instead of only tinting them.
  • Moods: save a complete look (shape, material, colors and corners) as a named Mood and switch between them in one click. Each display can wear its own, and a Mood can dress the desktop too, setting a matching wallpaper.
  • Quick Settings: the appearance editor, redesigned and renamed to say what it actually is. Change how the menu bar looks from the menu bar itself, without opening Settings.
  • Rounded screen corners: round the corners of any display, at the radius you pick.
  • Three menu bar styles on a single axis: Single, Paired and Sections. With Single and the inset off, the bar sits flush with the screen edge and gets its own bottom-corner control, including a flared edge.
  • The Sections pane has two shapes, and moving an item between sections no longer requires dragging it.
  • A Permissions page that tells you which access is missing, what it unlocks, and takes you straight to the right place in System Settings.
  • German, Spanish and Japanese are fully translated.

⚡ Improved

  • Menu bar scanning runs off the main thread, so the interface stays responsive while Glow works.
  • Item Search opens instantly: its list is built once, ahead of your first use.
  • Opening Sections no longer re-scans and reveals the whole menu bar every time, which was costing 4.7 seconds per open.
  • Glass Style in Simple mode now offers a trimmed set of finishes instead of an over-full list. Every variant is still there in Advanced.
  • Items in Floating now keep their own order, saved by Glow, so reordering there works without Full Disk Access.

🛠️ Fixed

  • Reordering menu bar items did nothing on macOS 27. macOS changed where it keeps item order during the 27 betas; Glow now writes to the right place. See Known Issues for the access it needs.
  • Turning off the Collapsible section moved all of its items to Floating with no way back: re-enabling it left the section permanently empty.
  • The menu bar came up fully expanded even when you had left it collapsed. The saved layout was only applied when something changed, never at startup.
  • The clock stopped opening Notification Center as soon as anything was hidden, whatever you hid.
  • "Show Overlay" did nothing: with two displays, all three scopes left both overlays visible.
  • The menu bar capsule was drawn at the wrong size on a display that is not hosting the menu bar.
  • Two rows could appear with the same icon, and Time Machine could show up as a VPN entry.
  • A layout that failed to apply was never retried, neither automatically nor from the Retry button.
  • Show on Hover could be dead after launch, and could trigger on a tremor at the edge of the reveal region instead of a real crossing into it.
  • Clicks could be swallowed by the GlowBar panel: the strip of menu bar beneath it went dead, and reopening the panel could take two clicks.
  • Fixed a stray capsule being drawn around a control that was no longer in the menu bar, and the section capsules taking a couple of seconds to appear on a second display.

⚠️ Known Issues

  • This release is for macOS 27. macOS 26 stays on the 2.x line until the unified build finishes testing.
  • On macOS 27, reordering items in the menu bar itself requires Full Disk Access, and so does the Collapsible section, because macOS keeps item order in a protected location. Glow tells you so in Permissions instead of silently doing nothing. Floating keeps its own order and works without the permission.
  • Glow is still being polished. This build ships on the stable channel because there is not yet a polished stable release, so expect frequent updates.

item.title: 3.0.0-beta.3
item.description:
This beta focuses on menu bar stability: item positioning, third-party icons, and overlay behavior on smaller displays.

🛠️ Fixed

  • Fixed occasional duplicate or misplaced icons for some third-party menu bar items.
  • Fixed positioning and ordering of items in the hidden section.
  • Fixed split menu bar capsules sometimes collapsing to zero width after capturing icons.
  • Fixed the menu bar overlay behaving incorrectly when switching desktops with a maximized window on smaller displays.

item.title: 2.2.0-beta.1
item.description:
This beta adds macOS 26 item spacing controls and Floating groups, along with reliability and performance improvements across menu bar scanning, layout, and appearance.

✨ New

  • Organize menu bar items into logical Floating groups, with full keyboard navigation and focus.
  • New macOS 26 item spacing controls and a custom Glow menu bar icon.

⚡ Improved

  • Faster, lower-memory menu bar scanning.
  • More reliable detection of Control Center–hosted menu bar items.
  • Smoother drag-and-drop placement between menu bar sections.
  • System spacing overrides are now reversible and recover cleanly from partial applies.

🛠️ Fixed

  • Fixed a startup loop that could repeatedly re-apply layout profiles.
  • Fixed menu bar item icons occasionally failing to refresh.
  • Fixed low-contrast Liquid Glass finishes in Simple mode by switching them to Frosted.
  • Fixed layout profiles incorrectly including system-managed menu bar items.
  • Fixed a rare crash caused by power and thermal notifications handled off the main thread.
  • Improved stability when the system reports invalid menu bar material values.

item.title: 3.0.0-beta.2
item.description:
A stability-focused beta that sharpens how Glow tracks, hides, and reorders your menu bar items — with fixes for cold-start icon leaks, third-party item identity, layout-editor dragging, and Item Search focus.

⚡ Improved

  • Sharper, more stable menu bar icon capture — including the clock — so icons no longer flicker or show the wrong crop.

🛠️ Fixed

  • Hidden menu bar icons no longer briefly leak into view right after launch.
  • Fixed items from some third-party apps whose icons could fluctuate or land in the wrong place when dragged.
  • Dragging items in the layout editor is now more reliable, with steadier identity and ordering.
  • Reordering items within the visible section now behaves as expected.
  • Item Search no longer steals keyboard focus from the app you’re using.

item.title: 3.0.0-beta.1
item.description:
First beta of Glow for macOS 27. Glow has been rebuilt from the ground up for the new menu bar in macOS 27. This build runs only on macOS 27.

✨ New

  • Native macOS 27 support: a menu-bar engine rewritten for how macOS 27 composites status items, so hiding, showing, and reordering work with the new system.
  • Layout presets: save menu-bar arrangements and switch between them.
  • More Liquid Glass options: new Alt Style and Tight Shadow looks for the capsules.
  • Clearer layout editor: Settings › Sections now shows the real menu-bar icons.

⚡ Improved

  • Icon thumbnails: menu-bar icons are captured more reliably and look sharper in the layout editor.
  • Menu-bar scanning: removed redundant rescans for a lighter, more responsive menu bar.

🛠️ Fixed

  • Fixed the hidden section not revealing on hover right after using the GlowBar toggle.
  • Fixed clicking a floating menu-bar item from GlowBar.
  • Fixed items such as Weather and Siri occasionally starting in the wrong section after launch.
  • Fixed the Sections editor becoming unusable when the chevron fell off a crowded menu bar.
  • Fixed cases where reordering menu-bar items did not take effect.
  • Fixed capsule materials flickering while sections merge or resize.
  • Fixed hover stopping working after the system temporarily disabled mouse monitoring.

⚠️ Known Issues

  • This is an early beta on a beta OS. Menu-bar item capture and reordering may occasionally need a relaunch. Please report anything odd.

✨ New

  • Smoother shape-merging transitions: added polished transitions when GlowBar or Item Search opens within a menu-bar section.

⚡ Improved

  • Liquid Glass capsules: their appearance now follows the selected Auto, Light, or Dark mode.
  • License and trial reliability: added a short offline grace period and clearer handling of revoked licenses versus temporary connection problems.
  • Responsiveness: improved the item layout editor and menu-bar startup path.

🛠️ Fixed

  • GlowBar flicker: fixed a flicker and occasional double-open when revealing GlowBar with the pointer.
  • Menu-bar segment merging: fixed layout and interaction issues while segments merge or change size.
  • Stale menu-bar widths: fixed widths that could appear after sections collapse, expand, or refresh.
  • GlowBar positioning: fixed positioning when no persistent menu-bar items are present.
  • Fullscreen overlay state: fixed cases where a fullscreen app or a transparent fullscreen overlay could leave Glow's overlay in the wrong state.
  • Startup hang: fixed a case where the app could remain unresponsive while waiting for the initial menu-bar item snapshot.
  • Layout editor drag errors: drag failures no longer show a blocking error dialog.
  • Accessibility permission recovery: fixed recovery when Accessibility permission is revoked while Glow is running.
